stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates continued community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest large language models.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: SpaceX intends to invest up to $100 billion in massive Louisiana spaceport
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: SpaceX plans a massive investment of up to $100 billion for a new spaceport in Louisiana.
The project is described as being of unprecedented scale and significance.
This signals a major expansion and commitment by SpaceX to large-scale infrastructure development.

stories.title: New bootloader lets you take the "Meta" out of the original Meta Quest
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: A new bootloader exploit has been discovered for the original Meta Quest device.
The vulnerability allows for privilege escalation, granting users 'full control' over the hardware.
This exploit effectively bypasses Meta's servers and proprietary applications on the headset.

stories.title: OpenAI Jalapeño: Better than Nvidia Blackwell
stories.author: bmulholland
bullet_points: OpenAI is reportedly developing custom AI chips, dubbed 'Jalapeño', designed to compete directly with high-end Nvidia hardware like Blackwell.
The news suggests OpenAI claims these proprietary chips can outperform current Nvidia processors in specific benchmarks.
This signals a major industry shift towards large tech companies building their own specialized AI silicon to reduce reliance on external suppliers.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The tags confirm its relevance to the broader transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama, indicating broader open-source adoption.
The model is a 30 billion parameter (3B active) open model specifically designed for persistent AI agents.
Its core functionality supports complex, multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling directly on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 models running in Ollama achieve significant speed improvements on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in its MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
This integration specifically targets and optimizes performance on Apple Silicon hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, signaling ongoing development.

stories.title: Lab supply companies have been selling antibodies using manipulated images
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Lab supply companies are found to be selling antibodies that utilize manipulated images.
The extent of the image manipulation is described as widespread among suppliers.
The quality of the fraudulent data is severe enough that it would warrant retraction in scientific publications.

stories.title: AI won’t replace radiologists, but it will dramatically change their jobs
stories.author: Lola Butcher, Knowable Magazine
bullet_points: AI is set to transform the role of radiologists rather than completely replace them.
The article references past predictions of full AI replacement, which have proven inaccurate.
The shift indicates AI will become a powerful augmentation tool in medical diagnostics.

stories.title: Apple's new desktop computers are designed specifically for local AI development
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Apple is specifically designing new desktop computers to support local AI development.
The hardware refresh addresses the community trend of users daisy-chaining Macs for AI workloads.
This signals a strategic shift by Apple to integrate and optimize for on-device, local AI processing.

stories.title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
stories.author: Yingcong Chen
bullet_points: Introduces 'ReWorld,' an interactive world model designed to handle long-horizon memory.
Addresses the structural conflict between control (short horizon) and memory (unbounded history) by separating these concerns during training.
Employs mixed per-head attention windows—local heads for recent context and global heads for full history—with random routing to ensure flexibility.

stories.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?
stories.author: Qinhuai Na
bullet_points: Introduces the SWE Refactor Bench to test coding agents on complex, long-horizon tasks like whole-repository stack migration.
Addresses a critical flaw in existing benchmarks: 'Blindness,' where agents pass tests by copying original code instead of performing actual migration.
Investigates the practical capability of AI agents to autonomously manage and resolve significant technical debt in large software systems.

stories.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?
stories.author: Qinhuai Na
bullet_points: Introduces the SWE Refactor Bench to test coding agents on complex, long-horizon tasks like whole-repository stack migration.
Addresses a critical limitation in current benchmarks: they only test behavioral correctness, allowing agents to 'cheat' by copying original code (Blindness).
The research aims to determine if autonomous coding agents can realistically handle the massive, complex task of modern software migration.

stories.title: FDA authorizes first wearable device that monitors ketone and blood sugar levels
stories.author: sunnynagra
bullet_points: FDA has approved a novel wearable device.
This device is capable of monitoring both ketone and blood sugar levels.
This represents a significant advancement in continuous, non-invasive health monitoring technology.

stories.title: Apple introduces M6 and M5 Ultra
stories.author: interpol_p
bullet_points: Apple has introduced new high-performance chips, specifically the M6 and M5 Ultra.
The announcement signals a significant advancement in Apple's silicon lineup.
Related coverage compares the new M6 Mac Mini to previous generations like the M4.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models and hardware.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: The world's busiest spaceport is about to get a lot quieter, at least for now
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX is planning to launch its Starship vehicle from a Florida spaceport.
The target launch timeframe is ambitious, with initial goals set for the end of the year.
The article suggests a more realistic timeline for Starship deployment is likely 2027.

stories.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
stories.author: Wee Sun Lee
bullet_points: Addresses the instability issues commonly found when training critics in reinforcement learning for large language models.
Introduces 'Best-Practice Critic Optimization (BPCO),' a new recipe designed to stabilize and improve critic training.
Proposes methods to estimate token-level advantages efficiently, potentially reducing the need for multiple response sampling.

stories.title: EG-ARSA: An Expert-Grounded Open Model for Visual Road Safety Auditing in Low-Resource Settings
stories.author: Moazzem Hossain
bullet_points: Introduces EG-ARSA, a novel AI framework designed for visual road safety auditing.
Addresses critical challenges in low-resource settings, such as limited data and lack of qualified auditors.
Utilizes Expert-Grounded Distillation (EGD) to transfer institutional road safety expertise into a compact vision-language model.

stories.title: Physics-Constrained Deep Learning Model for Contactless Blood Pressure Monitoring from Triaxial Bodyseismography
stories.author: Wenzhan Song
bullet_points: Introduces Phy-BP, a physics-constrained deep learning model for contactless blood pressure monitoring.
Addresses limitations of traditional Ballistocardiography (BCG) signals, such as vulnerability to body-bed interaction variations.
Aims to improve the generalizability and robustness of BP estimation by incorporating physical constraints into the deep learning framework.

stories.title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
stories.author: Sami Jaghouar
bullet_points: Prime Agent is an open-source harness designed to enable long-horizon agency in Language Models (RLMs).
It addresses the limitation of sequential processors by integrating external computation and information beyond model weights.
The system features a persistent IPython REPL for programmatic context processing and maintains state via a Continual Harness for memory and skill tracking.

stories.title: ConvergeFlow: Language Flow with Provable Convergence to Token Embeddings
stories.author: Gen Li
bullet_points: Introduces ConvergeFlow, a novel embedding-space flow-based Language Model (LM).
Addresses a key limitation in continuous LMs where flow trajectories don't guarantee termination at valid token embeddings.
Constrains the data predictor to the convex hull of token embeddings to ensure convergence.

stories.title: How AI Assistance Affects Human Skill Development: A Study of Learning with Logic Puzzles
stories.author: Padhraic Smyth
bullet_points: The study investigates the trade-off between short-term performance gains and long-term skill development when using AI assistance.
Findings suggest that frequent AI use, especially with low-cost assistance, may undermine human skill development over time.
The research utilized a controlled logic-puzzle experiment to examine how the cost of AI assistance influences its usage frequency.

stories.title: The Interaction Tax: When Communication Erases Diversity in Multi-Agent Teams
stories.author: Chenhao Tan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the conflicting findings regarding the utility of multi-agent LLM interaction.
Some studies show benefits from agent interaction (e.g., debate, critique loops), while others find it adds cost without quality improvement.
The authors suggest the contradiction stems from a lack of clear distinction in current research methodologies.

stories.title: Adapter-Based Few-Shot Continual Learning for Malicious Packet Recognition
stories.author: Andrew Arash Mahyari
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of catastrophic forgetting in continual learning for malware detection.
Focuses on Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning (FSCIL) to adapt to new malware variants with limited data.
Proposes an adapter-based approach to enable models to learn new threats without complete retraining.

stories.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
stories.author: Wee Sun Lee
bullet_points: Addresses the instability issues common in critic-based reinforcement learning for large language models.
Introduces 'Best-Practice Critic Optimization (BPCO)' as a new training recipe to improve critic stability and efficiency.
Proposes methods to estimate token-level advantages using single responses, moving beyond multi-sample approaches.

stories.title: ConvergeFlow: Language Flow with Provable Convergence to Token Embeddings
stories.author: Gen Li
bullet_points: Introduces ConvergeFlow, a novel embedding-space flow-based Language Model (LM).
Addresses a key limitation in continuous LMs where flow trajectories don't guarantee termination at valid token embeddings.
Constrains the data predictor to the convex hull of token embeddings to ensure convergence.

stories.title: Robustness of Anomaly Detection Models for Industrial Control Systems under Training-Time Data Contamination
stories.author: Li Yang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical vulnerability in industrial AI: the lack of robustness of anomaly detection models when training data is contaminated.
Focuses specifically on Industrial Control Systems (ICS), a high-stakes, critical infrastructure domain.
Evaluates model performance under various forms of training-time data corruption using the SWaT benchmark.

stories.title: Interpretable AI with Local Distillation
stories.author: Snigdha Panigrahi
bullet_points: The paper addresses the lack of interpretability in high-performing modern AI models (e.g., foundation models, gradient-boosted ensembles).
It proposes using local linear modeling as a method to achieve transparency without significantly sacrificing predictive accuracy.
The core idea is leveraging the local approximation of a smooth regression function by a linear fit near specific query points.

stories.title: MetaCaster: Meta-Harness-Optimized Agent for End-to-End Few-Shot Learning of Lightweight Time Series Forecasters
stories.author: Jingchao Ni
bullet_points: Addresses the resource inefficiency of using large foundation models for time series forecasting (TSF) in constrained environments.
Focuses on enabling lightweight, compact TSF models to perform effectively in few-shot learning scenarios.
Tackles the challenge of training lightweight models when scarce, privacy-sensitive, or slowly accumulated time series data is available.

stories.title: RAD: Rule-Augmented Relational Anomaly Detection
stories.author: Tyler Derr
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in relational anomaly detection where traditional methods flatten database tables, losing crucial structural context.
The proposed method, RAD, aims to preserve relational structure to better detect anomalies dependent on multi-hop dependencies.
A key challenge highlighted is the need to effectively incorporate symbolic behavior into relational anomaly detection models.

stories.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
stories.author: Wee Sun Lee
bullet_points: Addresses the instability issues inherent in training critics for reinforcement learning methods applied to Large Language Models (LLMs).
Introduces Best-Practice Critic Optimization (BPCO), a new recipe designed to stabilize and improve critic training efficiency.
Proposes methods to estimate token-level advantages from a single response, contrasting with multi-response sampling techniques.

stories.title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
stories.author: Sami Jaghouar
bullet_points: Introduces 'Prime Agent,' an open-source harness designed to enable long-horizon agency in Language Models (RLMs).
Addresses the limitation of sequential processors by integrating external information and computation beyond model weights.
Features a persistent IPython REPL for programmatic context processing and a Continual Harness for managing memory and skills across trajectories.

stories.title: ConvergeFlow: Language Flow with Provable Convergence to Token Embeddings
stories.author: Gen Li
bullet_points: Introduces ConvergeFlow, a novel embedding-space flow-based Language Model (LM).
Addresses a key limitation in continuous LMs: the lack of guaranteed convergence to valid token embeddings.
Constrains the data predictor to the convex hull of token embeddings to ensure proper termination.

stories.title: Mitigating Reasoning-Induced Misalignment via Safety-Direction Penalty
stories.author: Di Wang
bullet_points: The paper addresses 'Reasoning-Induced Misalignment' (RIM), a safety risk where LLMs trained on benign reasoning data can develop harmful behaviors.
RIM is a complex issue, as cross-architecture checks show it doesn't always manifest, and previous theories focused on neuron-level entanglement.
The research aims to identify the underlying geometry of the representation space to mitigate this misalignment using a 'Safety-Direction Penalty'.

stories.title: On the Threat Model of Weird Generalization and Emergent Misalignment
stories.author: William Walden
bullet_points: The paper investigates 'weird generalization' (WG), where narrow fine-tuning on small datasets causes unexpected, broad changes in model behavior.
The research aims to identify the specific features of fine-tuning data (e.g., size, composition, novelty) that are necessary for WG to occur.
This work contributes to understanding the threat models and potential misalignment risks associated with fine-tuning large language models.

stories.title: What's the Catch? Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Vision-Language Models
stories.author: Danae Sánchez Villegas
bullet_points: The research addresses a key limitation in Vision-Language Models (VLMs): the lack of guaranteed temporal structure understanding.
A novel evaluation framework, TimeCatch, is proposed to test temporal consistency by framing it as an anomaly detection problem.
The method introduces specific anomaly types, such as swapping consecutive frames or replacing frames with Gaussian noise, for controlled testing.

stories.title: How Useful are LLMs for Grammar Engineering? Cantonese ParGram Resources and Controlled Experimental Evaluation with English Baselines
stories.author: Chit-Fung Lam
bullet_points: The research evaluates the utility of Large Language Models (LLMs) for 'grammar engineering' in Cantonese.
New Cantonese ParGram resources were created and used as gold standards for controlled experimental evaluation.
GPT-5.4 demonstrated superior performance compared to gpt-oss-120b in generating machine-processable grammars.

stories.title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Arabic Natural Language Processing Research: Trends, Topic Evolution, and Research Gaps -- A Bibliometric and Topic-Based Study
stories.author: Mullosharaf K. Arabov
bullet_points: The study provides a comprehensive bibliometric and topic-based analysis of Arabic NLP research.
It analyzes a large dataset of 7,120 Arabic NLP papers published between 1960 and 2026.
The research aims to map trends, track topic evolution, and identify gaps in the field, utilizing BERTopic.

stories.title: Chat history is a second read path into your RAG data — gate the replay like the search
stories.author: rdiegoss
bullet_points: The article discusses using chat history as a secondary retrieval path for RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems.
It proposes implementing gating mechanisms for chat replay, similar to how search results are managed.
The context involves persisting source citation details (documents, scores, names) within a copilot's responses.

stories.title: The M5 Ultra Mac Studio: I Did the Math So You Don't Have To
stories.author: arshtechpro
bullet_points: Apple has announced the new Mac Studio lineup.
The new models feature the M5 Max and the debut of the M5 Ultra chip.
The article provides a technical analysis ('did the math') of the new hardware.

stories.title: Weir - deterministic unit tests for AI agents (no LLM)
stories.author: idogol24
bullet_points: Introduces 'Weir,' a tool for creating deterministic unit tests specifically for AI agents.
Addresses a critical security/reliability gap where agent logs might falsely report success despite internal failures or hijacking.
Highlights the capability to test agent logic without relying on large language models (LLMs) during testing.

stories.title: Half the Requests Wearing ChatGPT's Name Were Scanning Us for Secrets
stories.author: izgorodin
bullet_points: The article discusses the use of Cloudflare's AI Crawl Control feature.
It reveals that a significant portion of requests bearing ChatGPT's name were potentially scanning for sensitive information.
The content suggests a security or privacy concern related to AI scraping activities.
